grh_28969769b32d3409c223.title: Oh, Brothers!
paragraphs: Brothers Carl and Jerry Bernaschi both become interested in Mary Ann and quickly turn her into the latest subject of their lifelong rivalry. Each takes her out, tries to impress her and warns her about the other's faults, while Mary Ann watches their competition with growing amusement. When the brothers finally demand to know which of them she prefers, she reveals that neither one is her choice. She has fallen for the story's narrator, Stanley Perinaschi, whose running commentary has placed him closer to the action than the brothers realized. A year later Mary Ann and Stanley are happily married and expecting a child, while Carl and Jerry remain bachelors but are about to become honorary uncles.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on March 6, 1979. It is listed as episode 22 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Steven Keats, Waldo Byron, Tony Pope, and Corey Burton. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Mark Trella as writer, and Andy Griffith as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_2824064afc645f29988f.title: The Great Waltz
paragraphs: Young Johann Strauss wants to compose and conduct despite the opposition of his famous father, who expects him to choose a safer profession. When the elder Strauss is delayed, Johann gets an unexpected chance to conduct and proves himself with the music that will make him famous, including the Blue Danube. Father and son finally reconcile, with the elder Strauss acknowledging the younger man's gift shortly before his death and Johann accepting the musical inheritance he once had to fight for.

grh_2883d80fb3a4646731a2.title: Irene
paragraphs: Irene, a working girl from Ninth Avenue, meets wealthy Donald Marshall and is recruited to wear expensive clothes in public so fashionable society will discover a struggling dress shop. The Cinderella-like experiment turns Irene into the toast of Fifth Avenue, while false genealogy and her borrowed elegance convince society that she belongs among them. Irene's mother finally arrives and exposes the masquerade, insisting that her daughter come home and shed the fine feathers. Donald makes clear that the revelation has not changed his feelings: he is willing to wait until Irene decides he is good enough for her, which Irene and her mother recognize as a proposal.

grh_28b82a6911c9cd1a048d.title: Madame Sherry
paragraphs: Edward supports his dance school with money from Uncle Theophilus, who has been led to believe Edward has a wife. For the uncle's visit, Edward's housekeeper pretends to be Madame Sherry while Edward grows close to his young cousin Yvonne. grh_28532870cf37cf9ff45c.title: Hostages
paragraphs: During a violent hostage standoff, a separated police officer's wife realizes the crisis has put her directly in the path of her unstable husband. Years on the force have left him paranoid and violent, and she believes he is using the confrontation to eliminate her and other people he sees as enemies. A hostage's staged medical emergency moves one gunman toward surrender, but the officer intervenes despite the stand-down; the standoff ends in gunfire and his death while outsiders continue to regard him as a devoted husband and hero.
